_: What the foxlib-c console answers, as regexes over the bytes written back (PROTOCOL.md 'foxlib-c console'). console_test.py runs each command through the real console.c on the host (build/console_sim) AND through the page's FakeConsoleLink (js/device/console-device.js), so the fake cannot drift from the firmware. `advance_ms` is how long the virtual clock runs after the command; `c_only` marks replies the fake does not model (a bench action's late `ok`, the cycle log).

expect: files \| reload \| stop \| uid \| version \| reboot \| bootsel
^FOX template=morse-songs/\S+ foxlib=c-\S+ board=picofox-foxlibc uid=[0-9a-f]{16} cfg=ok radio=ok id=set freq=146\.565\r\n
\r\nrevision=3 si5351=ok carrier=\d+\.\d keyed=[01] attenuation=\d+ i2c_write_us=\d+ i2c_errors=\d+ core1=ok correction_ppm=-?\d+\.\d state=\d\r\n

cases.note: mid-cycle: the transmission stops, the value applies, the cycle restarts (the fake models the reply only)

expect: FOX template=morse-songs/\S+ foxlib=c-\S+ board=picofox-foxlibc uid=[0-9a-f]{16} cfg=ok radio=ok id=set freq=146\.565\r\n
^ok \(entering UF2 bootloader: the RPI-RP2 drive appears\)\r\n$

cases.note: F15: atten during a bench action stops it (answering it) and applies — core 1 refuses the write mid-stream, so core 0 stops first; the value used to be dropped while the console printed ok
F15: a reload during a bench action answers the action (ok (stopped)) so a waiting host is released
